subject: Next steps: Clarkson deployment pathway — Dedicated capacity HW and concurrency questions
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@clarkson.ai>, Priya Malhotra <priya@clarkson.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2026 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Recap + action items from today’s deployment discussion

Thanks again for the call today — great context from the Clarkson infra and product teams. Quick recap and the few follow-ups we need to size a Dedicated capacity proposal: 

1) Customer goals (from call)
- Primary: real-time chat assistant for product support (user queries + long-context retrieval)
- Target SLA: 95th-p < 220ms on text-gen critical paths; batch embeddings/async jobs can be higher latency

2) Traffic and token profile (we need confirmation)
- Alex mentioned expected sustained TPS ~3k for inference calls with spikes to ~6k during business hours. Please confirm hourly shape.
- Typical token mix estimate: 75% short prompts (<512 tokens), 20% mid (512–2k), 5% long (>2k, retrieval-heavy).

3) Deployment constraints
- Clarkson prefers a private network setup but is open to Redwood Dedicated if we can guarantee isolation and a VPC peering option.
- Compliance note: SOC2 is required; PCI not currently in scope.

4) Hardware and execution questions (actionable for sizing)
- GPU preference: you said H100 looks best for latency, but price sensitivity may push to an A100 or mixed fleet. Please confirm strict preference vs budget target.
- Concurrency target: how many concurrent sessions need sub-220ms? (we used 95th-p SLA above)
- Burst capacity: confirm expected burst-to-sustained ratio and duration (minutes).

5) Next steps / asks (attachments included)
- I attached a simple capacity matrix (clarkson_capacity_matrix.xlsx) and a short options brief (redwood-dedicated-options.pdf). Fill the matrix columns (hourly TPS, % long prompts, peak minute TPS) and send back.
- Proposed next meeting: technical deep-dive with Karthik and Ben — Nov 10 or Nov 11, 11:00–13:00 PT. Let us know what works.

If you prefer an on-prem evaluation instead of Dedicated, call that out and we’ll prepare private deploy notes.

Best,

Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: clarkson_capacity_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
Attachment: redwood-dedicated-options.pdf (1.8MB PDF stub)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@clarkson.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Malhotra <priya@clarkson.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + action items from today’s deployment discussion

Thanks, Marissa — appreciate the clear list. A few quick clarifications below: 

- Traffic: current prod-like estimate is sustained 3k TPS (avg) with peak 6k TPS for ~15–25 minutes during our peak window (14:00–15:00 PT). We can export a sample hourly CSV for the week.
- Token mix: your split is a good first cut. For long calls, the average prompt length is around 1.8k tokens; we do have a small cohort of >6k token workflows but that’s ~1% of traffic.
- GPU preference: performance-first teams prefer H100 for tail latency. Finance wants an A100-based POC first to compare unit-cost. Open to a hybrid approach.
- Concurrency: goal is to keep 95th-p latency <220ms for our interactive cohort of ~1.5k concurrent sessions during peak.

We’ll populate the capacity matrix and push it back to you by COB Nov 4. Also curious for a ballpark: what family of Dedicated pod counts would you initially hypothesize for the H100 vs A100 option based on these numbers?

Alex
Head of Platform | Clarkson AI
alex.j@clarkson.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@clarkson.ai>, Priya Malhotra <priya@clarkson.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 17:20:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Recap + action items from today’s deployment discussion

Perfect — thanks for that color, Alex. A few immediate sizing hypotheses and callouts while we review your CSV: 

- Hypothesis (quick): for the interactive cohort you described (~1.5k concurrent, 3k sustained TPS, 6k peak bursts), an H100-focused Dedicated pool in the 4–6 GPU range with autoscale to 8 GPUs for bursts is a reasonable starting point for strict latency targets. An A100 pool would likely require 6–10 GPUs for the same tail SLA or a hybrid approach where H100s serve the interactive tier and A100s handle background/async jobs.

- Cost / trade-off summary: H100 yields better 95th-p latency and smaller cluster size but higher per-hour cost. A100 is cheaper per-GPU but will need more units and careful batching to hit the same latency SLO. We’ll include estimated hourly burn ranges in the formal proposal.

- Token handling: for the small long-tail >6k token workflows, we recommend a separate service window (long-run jobs) routed to a quantized A100 pool to avoid polluting interactive SLAs; prefix/KV caching also helps for common retrieval patterns.

- Data plane: if Clarkson wants VPC-level isolation, Redwood Dedicated can be configured with VPC peering and strict ingress rules. If you require air-gapped on-prem, we’ll scope that separately (longer lead).

Next concrete asks from your side: CSV + any sample prompts you can share (anonymized) so Karthik can run a quick throughput/latency estimate. We’ll produce a short decision-ready proposal once we have the CSV.

Available deep-dive slots: Nov 10, 11:00 PT or Nov 11, 11:30 PT — which works?

Thanks — Marissa

Subject: Quick technical note before deep-dive

Alex / Priya — quick one from the infra side:

- If you can share ~500 anonymized sample prompts and a 24-hour TPS CSV (minute granularity), I can run a micro-benchmark and give an H100 vs A100 GPU count estimate (including expected 95th-p tail) within 48 hours. This will let us avoid overprovisioning in the initial proposal.
- Also, confirm whether the interactive sessions maintain KV cache across the session (that affects memory/KV sizing).

I can also spin up a quick throughput test harness against a short model sample if you’re willing to let us run a controlled benchmark (we’ll sign an NDA if needed).

—Karthik
